01 / TEACH LEGACY DENSE NETWORK

Legacy training studio

Paste an ASCII text corpus or load a .txt file. Nova predicts each next character from up to 64 preceding characters. Feed it varied sentences, paragraphs, and punctuation—not just repeated phrases.

— bytes
1–25 epochs · 40–250,000 ASCII bytes. Uses a 90/10 train/validation split; large corpora take longer.
Validation loss—
Validation next-char accuracy—
No active training session.0%

Weights are saved automatically each epoch and when stopped. v0.1.2 uses a new checkpoint because the 64-character encoder is incompatible with v0.1. Original v0.1 weights remain saved. Validation checks held-out characters, not genuine understanding.

02 / PROBE LEGACY DENSE BRAIN

Test legacy Nova

Type a short phrase or a longer sentence to light up the neurons. Nova considers at most the last 64 ASCII characters when predicting the next one.

Generated output will appear here.

This model sees up to 64 characters of context and predicts one of 128 ASCII characters. It is still a feed-forward character model—not a Transformer or conversational LLM. More varied sentences are learnable patterns, not proof of comprehension.

03 / TEACH LEGACY DENSE NETWORK

Legacy Dialogue School Comparison

A new kind of lesson: supply a user message and a desired Nova reply. Rust trains the neural weights to predict only the reply, using the question as context. There is no hardcoded answer lookup.

Teach Nova to reply

TAB-separated question / reply

One example per line: question [TAB] ideal response. Whole examples, not individual characters, are held out for validation. ASCII only; maximum 96 pairs.

Start with 3 epochs. This CPU-only dense network still has a 64-character context and limited conversational capability.
No dialogue lesson running.
Held-out reply loss—
Held-out char accuracy—

The last 20% of distinct question/reply pairs are reserved when at least five are provided. Low training loss means imitation; accuracy on unseen examples is a better (but still limited) signal.

Talk to Nova

Neural output only

Chat with the trained model. Each message is supplied as a single user turn; this version does not retain earlier dialogue inside its 64-character model context. Correct bad responses in the Teacher fields.

Start by training the dialogue lessons, then ask Nova something it has practiced—or a new question to test generalization.

Answers are generated character by character from the same trainable Rust network. This is a dialogue-learning prototype, not proof of language understanding or reliable reasoning.
